statements.quote: But as we push this technology forward, we must also take seriously our responsibility to rein in its potential harms — putting the right safeguards in place to ensure AI is used safely, ethically, and in the public interest.

record: Lead sponsor, with Senators Young, Rounds and Booker, of the reintroduced CREATE AI Act, which would establish the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource; the bill is about research access, not catastrophic risk.

Did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter from 17 senators urging President Trump to seek an AI agreement with China; the 17 signatures in the letter do not include him (his New Mexico colleague Ben Ray Luján did sign).

grade_reason: The only statement on AI found since 1 January 2025 is a general remark about reining in AI's 'potential harms' in a press release for a research-access bill. Nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk, and nothing dismisses it.
notes: Web search limit for the session was reached after nine searches; two further searches could not be run, so coverage of interviews, hearing remarks and floor speeches is thinner than intended and a reviewer may want to rerun. All five required search topics were run at least once. 23 September 2026 China letter: I extracted the text of the letter PDF and read all 17 signatures (Van Hollen, Kaine, Cortez Masto, Smith, Blumenthal, Merkley, Welch, Hirono, Padilla, Warnock, Luján, Murray, Rosen, Alsobrooks, Warren, Duckworth, Cantwell); Heinrich is not one. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found shows Heinrich as a co-sponsor; the Sanders summary sheet names only Sanders and Casar, news reports name only House co-sponsors, and the congress.gov co-sponsor page (S. 5493, bill number as given by Akin Gump, not independently confirmed) returned an access error, so non-co-sponsorship is not confirmed from the official record. The same 29 April 2026 press release contains the sentence "For both our economic and national security, we must harness AI's potential and mitigate its risks." but it comes after Heinrich's own quotation closes and appears to belong to another senator (likely Young), so it is not attributed to Heinrich. The press release date comes from the page's date field. His official site's AI-tagged press releases show only one 2025 item (5 May 2025, a request for public input on a science funding initiative, not opened) and November 2026 releases about data centers on public lands and electricity bills, which are out of scope (level D topics) and were not opened. Pre-2025 material (2023 AI Insight Forums, including the one on doomsday scenarios, the 2024 Senate AI roadmap, and a January 2024 call to fund the AI Safety Institute) is outside the date range and was not used. Politico's 23 September 2026 article on the China letter could not be opened.
